A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DPH-RL research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original SQL and mathematical-reasoning experiments, divergence ablations, training trajectories, and analyses of solution styles and knowledge retention.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in its main text and appendices. The separately attributed BIRD-Bench scores are additional comparison evidence.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 adds a final fresh sample for each near-perfect query, retaining it only if that sample is correct and otherwise discarding or transferring the query to D_exp. v1 describes saving a correct response without this rejection step. The exploration loss, divergence objectives, and combined DPH-RL loss remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions train on BIRD and filtered DAPO-17K data and evaluate SQL, mathematical reasoning, SQL-to-math transfer, and multiple solution styles. Spider and the seven math benchmarks are retained. The 32B experiment and style analysis already appear in v1's appendices.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds Infly-RL-SQL-32B, XiYanSQL-QwenCoder-32B, Arctic-ExCoT-70B, and Command A to the BIRD comparison. Their scores are explicitly attributed to BIRD Bench, rather than presented as new author-run experiments. The existing GRPO, DAPO, RKL, and divergence comparator sets are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: The configuration table changes RKL's online data from D_exp alone to D_exp plus D_pef. The hyperparameter table changes rollout temperature for both math models from 0.7 to 1.0, while budgets, dataset sizes, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. These are reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The divergence and eta ablations, Generator-versus-Divergence-Definition comparison, training-progress plots, retention/exploration analysis, style experiment, and SQL/math cases are retained. Their relocation or redrawing does not introduce a new analysis. No separate experiment tests the newly stated sampling refinement.

E5.justification: v1 Table 2 explicitly says results are averaged over three experimental runs described as inferences; the corresponding v2 Table 1 omits this statement. Both versions retain three reinforcement-learning training runs, Figure 6's error bars, and selection by highest BIRD Pass@16. No increased run count or new uncertainty procedure is established.

E6.justification: The retained SQL and math table entries match numerically. v2 adds BIRD Greedy scores of 70.1, 67.0, 68.5, and 63.5 for its four new external comparators. It also corrects the prose describing DPH-JS's BIRD Pass@8 advantage over DAPO to 3.3 percentage points, consistent with 70.5 minus 67.2.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 replaces squared divergence penalties in Theorem 1 with linear KL/f-divergence terms and a divergence-dependent constant. It explicitly defines the conditional reference policy on D_pef and D_exp. Appendix I substantially replaces v1 Appendix G's Pinsker/JS derivation, changes the supporting lemma, removes a separate lemma, and explains the coupling-to-divergence connection.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the empirical claim from improving both Pass@1 and Pass@k in and out of domain to improving these metrics in domain and preventing forgetting out of domain. The conclusion newly specifies computational costs comparable to GRPO. The central divergence-as-rehearsal contribution remains intact.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit limitations concerning dependence on base-model capabilities and estimation bias when learning from imperfect data. It expands the interpretation of the theoretical bonus and its reduction on exploration data, while removing the earlier prompt-adaptation explanation for Llama versus OmniSQL. The rewritten small-eta discussion also says DAPO on D_pef, which conflicts with the retained exploration-loss formulation.

D1.justification: v2 specifies near-perfect thresholds of 6 correct responses out of 8 for Llama and 7 out of 8 for Qwen. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit instructions to store reference log probabilities and its dataset-record formats. It adds reproducibility and LLM-assistance disclosures; hardware, framework, and code-access destination remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work substantially expand positioning around entropy control, high-entropy tokens, rollout adaptation, and hybrid SFT/RL, adding works such as SEED-GRPO, Polaris, and UFT. They remove the SAC discussion and several earlier RL-system references. The distinction from offline f-PO remains, while complementarity with entropy and reward approaches receives greater emphasis.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the introduction, related work, method motivation, experimental discussion, and conclusion. It consolidates experiment subsections, reorders the retention and training-progress analyses, restructures the appendices, and adds reproducibility and LLM-use sections. These are substantial narrative and organizational changes beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: The appendix style-count bars become main-text pie charts; the 32B results move into the main text with comparator rows; and the divergence-definition table moves into an appendix. Figure 1's labels and caption change, error-bar plots shrink, and the case studies are enlarged and reformatted across multiple pages. These substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 provides clearer organization and research positioning, explicit partition thresholds, a narrower out-of-domain claim, and more concrete limitations. These offer a limited net quality gain. The largely unchanged experimental evidence, lost inference-averaging and log-probability-storage details, and inconsistent small-eta explanation temper that gain. The substantial theoretical rewrite alone does not establish improved mathematical validity.
